newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums hit by mild weather, demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums hit by mild weather, demand.

text.p: NWE gas oil firmed slightly in line with benchmark IPE futures but thin demand helped keep pressure on heating oil and diesel premiums, traders said.
November IPE futures ended 50 cents firmer at $224.50 a tonne in scattered, featureless trade.
Traders said low sulphur diesel cargoes recently arrived in Europe from the United States and Algeria combined with continuing mild weather were weighing on premiums.
Buying interest in heating oil, desultory early in the week, has quickened but traded volumes remain modest with several purchasers holding off in hopes of lower prices.
Several traders said both diesel and heating oil premiums have the potential to strenghten sharply because refineries were running at capacity and stocks remained historically low.
A cargo of Algerian traded at Nov IPE +$24 cif NWE, up to $1 lower. A cargo of Russian was done at Nov IPE +$1.50 cif NWE, unchanged.
In barges, a parcel of heating oil refinery grade was traded at Nov IPE +$2 fob ARA. Diesel was Nov IPE +$23/26.
